headline: OpenFrontiers separates mathematical rediscovery from retrieval of known solutions
summary: Jiarui Yao, Ruida Wang and Tong Zhang introduce OpenFrontiers, a research-problem corpus of 12,151 records and a retrospective mathematics benchmark of 200 problems. The benchmark separates 110 problems with located 2026 solutions from 90 listed as open at the authors’ status check, and supplies a Lean 4 statement for each item. In an author-reported evaluation of seven LLM agents on a selected 50-item subset, closed-book agents solved at most 7 of 40 resolved items; most live-web successes followed retrieval of an existing solution. This is a paper-reported benchmark result, not independent evidence about general scientific ability. The corpus is 93.4% mathematics, nearly half its records are marked unassessed, and 1,562 of its 1,946 Lean attachments contain a lexical placeholder flag. The authors state that uncertain upstream status is retained rather than treated as proof a problem remains open.
